subject: MoE repack eligibility at the real artifact's quants: gate_up yes, down structurally impossible
method: GGUF metadata scan (scan_gguf) of the 30 expert layers, then the repack registry's own GGUFRepackShape.validate constraints applied per tensor

ffn_gate_up_exps.weight.why: rank 3, out_features 1408 divisible by 16, in_features 2816 divisible by 256 so bytes_per_row 1584 is a multiple of the Q4_K block (144)

ffn_down_exps.weight.why: no t16 repack shape is registered for Q5_1 at all; the single Q8_0 layer's shape is rank 2 (dense) and in_features 704 is not divisible by 256

structural_conclusion: Q4_K's block is 256 elements, so a 704-element row cannot be Q4_K at all; the down projection is Q5_1 (block 32) because that is what can represent it. The t16 Q4_K decode route can therefore never cover ffn_down_exps. The repack's ceiling is ffn_gate_up_exps: 59.8% of the MoE's 14.42 GB of expert weights.
corrections_to_campaign_record: Iteration 31's microbench measured a Q4_K chain at ffn 768 (a 9%-wider substitute for gate_up's 1408) and a Q4_K down arm, but the production down projection is Q5_1. The down projection - 40% of the MoE's expert bytes - has no production-shaped bandwidth measurement.
The campaign treats 'the MoE' as one quant. It is two: ffn_gate_up_exps Q4_K and ffn_down_exps Q5_1.
next_step: The t16 measurement stays the next candidate, scoped to gate_up's real shape (hidden 2816, ffn 1408). The down projection is already on the fastest registered decode path (gguf_q5_1 resolves to selected_gemv_bf16_bf16_out per iteration 33), so its remaining headroom is a Q5_1-specific question, not a repack one.
